acceptable_extra.why: The /user/<id> route returns any user's email with no authentication. Legitimate find in the code as written, so it does not count as a false positive. Rated Low or Medium for the loopback bind, High if the run argues the WSGI deployment never runs that bind line.

acceptable_extra.anchor: "SELECT id, title FROM posts WHERE title LIKE ?"
acceptable_extra.why: No LIMIT on search results. Argueable and low value here, since an empty q already returns everything. Does not count as a false positive, but a run that reports only this and claims the file is otherwise safe has missed the point of the fixture.

notes: The fixture is correct in every category it is labelled for: bound queries, env-based secret with no fallback, secure cookie flags, debug off. A correct run reports zero findings of the labelled kind, lists what it checked, and never claims the code is 'secure' or 'safe'. Reporting the /user/<id> authorization gap is legitimate and expected of a careful run - the original label calling any finding a false positive was wrong.
